edits.before: A full compiler can be written and Turing-completeness could be readily proven from the model as already presented.
edits.after: A full compiler can be written. Turing-completeness holds for the idealized machine with unbounded code memory initialized with a repeating blank-cell template, in which each cell encodes its symbol in the displacement of one jump and write-only handlers rewrite it. For a finite image the simulation is exact while the head stays inside the image, and the machine faults when it leaves.

edits.before: First of all, no registers are used in the instructions, and only jumps and data movement instructions are used.
edits.after: No Write-Execute procedure uses the stack: each executed instruction is an immediate store into an instruction field, a direct jump, or a no-operation. Registers and returns occur only in the C-calling-convention entry points, which patch the argument fields and return the result.

edits.before: It also requires a 64-bit divisor divided by a 32-bit dividend with a 32-bit remainder. Although the quotient cannot overflow 32-bits of output, the remainder potentially can.
edits.after: It also requires a 64-bit dividend divided by a 32-bit divisor with a 32-bit remainder. The remainder always fits in 32 bits, but the quotient overflows 32 bits unless the high half of the dividend is less than the divisor, which holds when both factors are first reduced modulo the divisor.
